suppressions.candidate: A stale session could retain access after the account is deactivated or its role changes.
suppressions.note: requireStaff resolves the session only to identify the row, then fetches id, email, role, and ativo from admin_users for every protected call; missing and inactive rows are rejected before capability dispatch.

suppressions.candidate: The Secretariat application list could deliver finance or applicant-evidence data by using a broad query.
suppressions.note: The Secretariat branch uses explicit application and student column allowlists at the database boundary, before the client receives the list.

suppressions.candidate: The Secretariat donor list could deliver CPF, address, CEP, or receipt metadata.
suppressions.note: The role-specific donor query selects operational fields only and omits CPF, address, CEP, receipt path, and receipt name at query time.

suppressions.candidate: A Secretariat caller could obtain an applicant-evidence ticket by submitting a known storage path.
suppressions.note: getDocumentUrl is still behind requireAuth, whose implementation resolves requireAdmin, while the only Secretariat final-document route is the separate persisted-ID action.

suppressions.candidate: A Secretariat user could download an old final-document version or a contract for a rejected application by guessing an ID.
suppressions.note: The action resolves the ID server-side and, for Secretaria, compares it to getCurrentIssuedDocuments. That lookup suppresses all pending documents and contracts for rejected applications, and returns only the latest version per kind.

suppressions.candidate: An anonymous caller could mint an upload ticket with traversal, arbitrary category, or dot-segment path.
suppressions.note: Categories are a fixed allowlist plus tightly indexed student patterns; filenames are sanitized and reject dot segments; the signed path is generated server-side under a fresh pending/{uuid} namespace. The storage driver independently enforces root containment.

suppressions.candidate: An uploaded HTML filename might execute in an Administrator browser when downloaded.
suppressions.note: guessMimeType returns application/octet-stream for every non-PDF/image extension, and the preview control is rendered only for database rows labeled application/pdf. An HTML payload named .pdf is delivered as application/pdf and does not create a browser HTML execution path.
